title: Book One · Chapter 41: Not This Afternoon
story:
Ronan keeps Saturday afternoon free for the street map. He finds a large piece of paper and puts two pencils beside it. One is Leo's usual dark pencil. The other has a soft blue end.

At school on Friday, he tells Leo to come after lunch.

“I can't,” Leo says. “I'm playing at Jun's.”

Ronan looks at him. “When did you plan that?”

“His mum asked my mum yesterday.”

“We were doing the map.”

“We didn't say Saturday.”

They did not choose Saturday together. Ronan asked for Leo's string first. Then he took it. This time he did not ask first. He just planned the afternoon for both of them.

“Can I come?”

“I don't know. It's Jun's home.”

Ronan feels left out. Ronan looks at the book in his hand and pretends to search for a page.

At pickup time, Jun invites another child to see his new paper game. Ronan waits a short distance away. No one asks him. Mum sees his face on the way home but lets him begin.

“Leo doesn't want the map.”

“Did he say that?”

“He wants Jun.”

“For one afternoon?”

Ronan kicks a loose leaf. It sticks to his shoe. Ronan stops and peels it off.

On Saturday, the big paper stays empty until after lunch. Dad is fixing a loose chair joint for Mrs Lan. Mum is going to buy thread. Ronan asks to go with her.

They take the partly finished map. At the thread shop, Mum needs to compare two greys in the daylight. The shopkeeper shows Mum two greys. She lets Ronan hold those two reels. He cannot touch all the other thread.

“This one looks blue,” he says.

“Beside that shirt, yes,” Mum says.

Outside, Ronan adds the thread shop to the map. He notices a narrow doorway. It is not on the map yet. He notices a small step at the entrance and puts a mark beside it.

“Why the step?” Mum asks.

“People can see the step on our map. Then they know to lift their feet.”

“Make the mark clear. You can read your mark. I need a clear word beside it, too.”

They stop at a little square. Three old men are playing a board game there. Ronan watches from beside Mum. He does not understand the game. But he likes its sounds. The men tap each piece on the wooden board.

One man points to a piece. “This one must wait,” he says. Another man laughs. “It waited a long time already!” All three laugh, and the game goes on.

They leave the square together. Ronan asks Mum a question. “Should I ask someone else to draw with me?”

“You could,” she says. “Choose your friend first. Do you want time with Jun? Or time with Mei? Jun likes different things from Leo. Mei likes different things, too.”

He thinks about Jun's paper games and Mei's drawings. Either could bring something different. He does not send another invitation today. He has new things for his map. He wants time to draw those. Then he can show Dad.

At home, the chair glue is dry. Dad lets Ronan test the chair. It doesn't move. Ronan sits with both feet off the ground and pretends to be an important visitor.

On Monday, Leo asks about the map. Ronan shows the thread shop and the step.

“You did more,” Leo says.

“Yes.”

“Can I add Jun's lane?”

“Yes. Please ask first. Do not draw over my lines.”

Leo asks. Ronan gives him the dark pencil. Ronan can tell Leo about Saturday now. Leo can tell Ronan about his own afternoon, too. They can finish the map another day. Leo opens his page beside Ronan's. There is room for both.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：free＝有空的；thread＝线；entrance＝入口；invitation＝邀请。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 为什么以为 Leo 一定会陪他画街图？
2. 他后来怎样度过原本留给 Leo 的下午？
